prompt: Match each technique to what it does.
hint: One of them leaves nothing to recover.

pairs.right: hides part of a value when shown
a code for the person, records still join
nobody can be singled out by reasonable means

prompt: Under the LGPD, which of the four techniques produces data that is no longer personal data?

choices.text: Pseudonymisation, when the key is kept in a KMS
choices.why: No. Ipê holds the key, so the data is still personal.

choices.text: Masking, because the value is hidden
choices.why: No. The full value is still in the table.

choices.text: Anonymisation, and only while it holds
choices.why: Right. Masked, tokenised and pseudonymised data stay personal data in full.

choices.text: Tokenisation, because the token is random
choices.why: No. Whoever controls the vault can map it back.

prompt: Which need is best served by masking?

choices.text: Support recognising a customer on the phone
choices.why: Right. Enough to confirm, not enough to copy.

choices.text: Analysts joining a customer's orders over a year
choices.why: No. That is a pseudonym's job.

choices.text: A public report on prescriptions by city
choices.why: No. A report needs counts nobody can be found in.

choices.text: Finding a customer by CPF in the database
choices.why: No. That needs a searchable stand-in.

prompt: The support view runs as its owner and so skips the table's row policy. How does Carla still see only her states through it?

choices.text: security_barrier applies the table's policy
choices.why: No. security_barrier controls the order conditions run in; it applies no policy.

choices.text: The view filters by agent_regions itself
choices.why: Right. current_user in a view is the person reading, so the rule moves into the view.

choices.text: The mask functions refuse other states
choices.why: No. They only change how a value is shown.

choices.text: She does not; she sees all 6,012
choices.why: No. The count through the view was 3,386.

prompt: Why was Carla first refused with `permission denied for function mask_cpf`?

choices.text: Functions cannot be used inside views
choices.why: No. One grant later, the same view worked.

choices.text: mask_cpf was written with a bug
choices.why: No. It worked as soon as it was granted.

choices.text: New functions are closed to PUBLIC by default
choices.why: Right. Lesson 2 revoked EXECUTE from PUBLIC for every function ipe_owner creates.

choices.text: Carla's token in OpenBao had expired
choices.why: No. This is a database privilege, not OpenBao.

prompt: A masked view shows `***.874.168-**`. What does masking NOT protect against?

choices.text: A screenshot of support's screen
choices.why: No. That is exactly what masking is for.

choices.text: An agent copying the number onto a note
choices.why: No. The agent sees only seven digits.

choices.text: A report printed from the view
choices.why: No. The report prints what the view shows.

choices.text: A backup of the table under it
choices.why: Right. The table still held every CPF in clear; masking changes only what is shown.

prompt: Which decisions in the developers' copy keep it useful while removing who people are? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Keeping customer_id so other tables still join
choices.why: Yes. A developer can still find the customer with sixty orders.

choices.text: Keeping the year of birth and losing the day
choices.why: Yes. Age-based features stay testable.

choices.text: Keeping the full CEP so delivery code is realistic
choices.why: No. The CEP kept only its first two digits.

choices.text: Copying the CPF with its check digits fixed
choices.why: No. The CPF was not exported at all.

prompt: Why is the masked developers' copy still personal data?
hint: What can it be joined to, and what do its columns say together?

choices.text: Because it has a header line
choices.why: No. A header names columns, not people.

choices.text: It joins back, and singles people out
choices.why: Right. Its ids join to production, and city, sex, year of birth and sign-up time identify many customers together.

choices.text: Because the names are only replaced, not removed
choices.why: No. 'Customer 1' names nobody.

choices.text: Because CSV files are personal data by law
choices.why: No. The format decides nothing.

prompt: How many lines did `wc -l` count in `dev_customers.csv`?
What does `card_token` let Ipê do without ever holding a card number?

choices.text: Read the card number when a customer asks
choices.why: No. Only the provider's vault can map the token back.

choices.text: Charge or refund the card through the provider
choices.why: Right. The token is a reference the provider honours.

choices.text: Compute the card number from the token
choices.why: No. A token has no computable relation to the value.

choices.text: Skip encryption on the payments table
choices.why: No. Tokens reduce risk; they do not replace the other layers.

prompt: What does tokenising card numbers change about PCI DSS for Ipê's database?
hint: Scope is about what a system stores, processes or transmits.

choices.text: Nothing; every database of a shop is in scope
choices.why: No. Scope follows card numbers, and the database never sees one.

choices.text: It moves the database into a stricter scope
choices.why: No. It moves it out.

choices.text: It makes the provider's vault out of scope
choices.why: No. The vault holds the numbers, so it is in scope.

choices.text: The database, backups and analysts fall out of scope
choices.why: Right. Never receiving a card number keeps them out.

prompt: Why can an HMAC from OpenBao be searched while a transit ciphertext cannot?
hint: Compare the two HMACs of the same CPF.

choices.text: Equal CPFs give equal HMACs
choices.why: Right. Encryption adds a random nonce, so two ciphertexts of one CPF differ.

choices.text: HMACs are shorter
choices.why: No. Length is not what makes a value searchable.

choices.text: HMACs can be decrypted by the database
choices.why: No. Nothing decrypts an HMAC; it is one-way.

choices.text: The index stores the CPF beside the HMAC
choices.why: No. The index holds only HMACs.

prompt: Why is an unkeyed hash of a CPF not a safe stand-in?

choices.text: Hashes collide too often for CPFs
choices.why: No. Collisions are not the problem.

choices.text: Hashes are reversible by design
choices.why: No. They are one-way; the issue is how few inputs there are.

choices.text: Every CPF can be hashed and compared in an afternoon
choices.why: Right. Eleven digits is a small space for a computer.

choices.text: PostgreSQL cannot index a hash
choices.why: No. It indexes any text.

prompt: How many HMACs appeared more than once when the unique index was refused?
Support needs to read a CPF back to a customer. Why can it not use `cpf_hmac` for that?
hint: What can be done with a one-way stand-in?

choices.text: The HMAC is masked in the view
choices.why: No. The view shows the HMAC whole.

choices.text: Support's token lacks the HMAC path
choices.why: No. Its policy has that path.

choices.text: HMACs expire after an hour
choices.why: No. The token expires; the HMAC does not.

choices.text: It is one-way; cpf_ct is decrypted
choices.why: Right. Two columns, two jobs: one to find, one to read.

prompt: Why did `customer_profile`, which never showed a CPF, block dropping the column?

choices.text: Its inner query said c.*
choices.why: Right. A * in a view is a dependency on every column; naming the columns removed it.

choices.text: Views always depend on every column of their tables
choices.why: No. Only on the columns they name, or all of them through *.

choices.text: The age band was computed from the CPF
choices.why: No. It was computed from birth_date.

choices.text: Analysts had a grant on the cpf column
choices.why: No. Grants do not block dropping a column.

prompt: Put the steps of finding Paula by the CPF she reads out in order.
hint: The database never sees the CPF.
items: The customer reads out the CPF
The support application asks OpenBao for its HMAC
The view is searched by cpf_hmac

prompt: After the drop, which of these still holds a CPF in clear anywhere in Ipê's systems?
hint: Think about copies made before today.

choices.text: A dump of sales.customers taken after the drop
choices.why: No. The column no longer exists to be dumped.

choices.text: The cpf_hmac index
choices.why: No. It holds HMACs, from which no CPF can be computed.

choices.text: A backup taken before the drop
choices.why: Right. Dropping a column changes the database, not its old copies; lesson 10 deals with them.

choices.text: The support view customer_card
choices.why: No. It shows the HMAC and the ciphertext.

prompt: The draft export replaced customer_id with its MD5. How did one command undo it?

choices.text: MD5 has a known inverse function
choices.why: No. It has none; the space of ids was simply tiny.

choices.text: It hashed ids 1 to 6,012 and compared
choices.why: Right. An unkeyed hash of a small, known range is the value written differently.

choices.text: It read the mapping from the database
choices.why: No. It needed no mapping at all.

choices.text: It asked OpenBao to decrypt the MD5
choices.why: No. OpenBao was never involved.

prompt: Why does the analytics pseudonym use its own key, `ipe-analytics-ref`, rather than `ipe-cpf-index`?

choices.text: ipe-cpf-index cannot compute HMACs of numbers
choices.why: No. It computes an HMAC of any input.

choices.text: Analysts are not allowed to read OpenBao keys
choices.why: No. Nobody reads either key.

choices.text: To keep the two purposes from joining
choices.why: Right. An analytics export can then never be joined to the support index: one key per purpose keeps the pseudonyms apart.

choices.text: Keys can only be used by one policy
choices.why: No. A key can be named in several policies.

prompt: Under the LGPD, pseudonymised data remains ___ data, because the controller holds the information that links it back.
With birth date, sex and CEP released, how many of the 6,012 customers were alone in their group?
hint: The first line of the result.

prompt: What makes a column a quasi-identifier?

choices.text: It holds a government number
choices.why: No. That is a direct identifier.

choices.text: It is encrypted
choices.why: No. Encryption has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Harmless alone, identifying together
choices.why: Right. Birth date, sex and postcode are the classic three.

choices.text: It is the sensitive value the release is about
choices.why: No. The sensitive value is what quasi-identifiers would expose.

prompt: Order the three releases from most customers alone in their group to fewest.
The release by decade, sex and state had 61 groups smaller than 5. Is it 5-anonymous?
hint: Every group needs at least k people.

choices.text: Yes, because only 22 customers are alone
choices.why: No. k = 5 asks for groups of five, not just no groups of one.

choices.text: No; its smallest group has one person
choices.why: Right. It needs more generalisation or suppression.

choices.text: Yes, because there are 246 groups
choices.why: No. The number of groups says nothing about their sizes.

choices.text: It cannot be measured without names
choices.why: No. It was measured, with no names.

prompt: Every customer in a 5-anonymous group bought the same psychiatric medicine. What does k-anonymity fail to prevent?
hint: You do not need the row to learn the value.

choices.text: Finding each person's exact row in the release
choices.why: No. That is what the group of five does prevent.

choices.text: Counting the group
choices.why: No. Counting is harmless here.

choices.text: Joining two releases made at different times
choices.why: No. That is a different weakness, also real.

choices.text: The medicine of anyone known to be in it
choices.why: Right. l-diversity asks that the sensitive values in a group vary.

prompt: How many groups did the decade, sex and state release have in all?
The regional report suppresses counts under 10 but also prints the national total. What goes wrong?

choices.text: The total gives them back
choices.why: Right. Subtracting the published cells from the total recovers the suppressed ones; with one suppressed cell, that cell exactly.

choices.text: The total is always below the threshold
choices.why: No. The total is the largest number in the report.

choices.text: Nothing; totals are anonymous
choices.why: No. A total with the other cells gives the hidden ones back.

choices.text: The report becomes too long
choices.why: No. Length is not the problem.

prompt: How many cities in the June report were shown as `<10`?
Under article 12 of the LGPD, when is anonymised data treated as personal data again?
hint: Two conditions, one about own means, one about reasonable effort.

choices.text: When it is stored outside Brazil
choices.why: No. Location is a transfer question, not an anonymisation one.

choices.text: When it is older than five years
choices.why: No. Age has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: When it is reversed by own means, or reversible with reasonable effort
choices.why: Right. Cost and time to reverse, with the technology available, decide what is reasonable.

choices.text: Never; once anonymised, always anonymised
choices.why: No. The law ties it to reasonable means at the time.

prompt: A dataset was anonymous when released. Two years later, a new public dataset makes joining it cheap. What is it now?
hint: At the time of the processing.

choices.text: Still anonymous, because it was when released
choices.why: No. The test is the means available at the time of processing, and the time moved.

choices.text: Possibly personal data again
choices.why: Right. Releases are re-examined, not certified once.

choices.text: Illegal to hold at all
choices.why: No. Personal data can be held with a legal basis.

choices.text: Sensitive data under article 11
choices.why: No. Re-identifiable does not mean sensitive.

prompt: Match each request to the technique that serves it.
hint: Who needs what from the data?

prompt: A partner asks for 'anonymised' order data with each customer's year of birth, sex, city and the full list of products. What is the right first answer?
hint: Measure before you call it anything.

choices.text: Send it; there are no names or CPFs
choices.why: No. 670 customers were alone on year, sex and city alone, before adding any product.

choices.text: Encrypt the file and send it
choices.why: No. The partner decrypts it and has exactly the same data.

choices.text: Ask whether counts would do, and measure any rows before sending
choices.why: Right. Treat it as personal data until a measurement says otherwise.

choices.text: Replace customer_id with its MD5 and send
choices.why: No. Section 8 reversed that in one command.
